replies.author: @majorronaldmandell7835
replies.text:
@J@Jetmab04:  You ask what are some reasons that people of the US Territories do not vote for US Presidents.   You could Google it up, but one reason for this is because the US voting system is not one  man, one vote.  Instead each state is given a number of voting delegates based upon its population, and it would be grossly unfair to award a territory with a total population of 20,000 souls even one delegate when each of the states are required to have 100s of thousands of people for each of their voting delegates.  

I might add that living out here on the US Territory of Guam as I do, and having lived for 12 years in the US Territory of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, that voting for President is a non issue with us.  We are disassociated from Federal politics, do not follow Federal politics or the issues involved because few Federal issues affect us, and nobody is concerned about voting for president, nobody misses voting for president, nobody feels deprived, and nobody wants to be bothered with it.  There are no Democrats or Republicans in the territories, and if you were to ask the vast majority of residents If they were conservatives or liberals, they would tell you that they didn’t know, or ask you what you mean.  

One cannot judge the wants and desires of the people living in the territories located thousands of miles away from the US proper with your own wants and desires on the mainland.   Also, I might mention that each of the territories have an elected delegate sitting in Congress, and thus are well represented.  

Finally, in case you are feeling sorry for the poor, mistreated, downtrodden people living out here, we receive more Federal funding per capita each year than any US state does (so much so that the people of some territories do not work, have never worked, and never will work), we do not pay Federal income tax, and depending upon the territory are thankfully exempted from certain provisions of the US Constitution, and have Native American status just as the Navahos, and Black Feet do, bringing with it all of the additional benefits, exemptions, and millions of dollars associated with that status.
